name: Multi-World Landing & Exploration
particleExperimentIntegrator: bounded semi-implicit Euler with mode-specific substeps
trajectoryModel: bounded one-way test-particle prediction: major gravity sources mutually evolve with velocity-Verlet while the prediction probe feels them without back-reaction; local probe/major-pair timestep caps are CPU-bounded and explicitly report accuracyLimited when the step budget cannot honor the preferred resolution
cosmicPhenomena: white-dwarf and brown-dwarf physical lab presets
compactObjectSafety: propulsion-safe stand-off + adaptive ship strong-gravity steps + adaptive close massive-body pair timestep ceiling + black-hole/neutron-star model guards + 10% c speed guard
cosmicObservation: massless frame/orbit views + physical bounded-thrust rendezvous to anchored phenomena
flightComputer: propulsion-safe target-relative approach with braking-safe velocity envelope + persistent station-keeping hold + STOP RELATIVE + TURN & BURN + physical inertial brake + prograde/retrograde attitude aids
fragmentPolicy: max 2 representative mutually gravitating impact fragments per event, 16 total resolved fragments, family cascade suppression; representative ejecta is generated in the collision center-of-mass frame with target recoil so represented linear momentum is conserved and fragment/recoil kinetic energy is capped to a configured fraction of available COM impact energy
navigationNumerics: adaptive ship strong-gravity substeps + adaptive massive-body pair encounter/crossing timestep ceiling + 10% c Newtonian validity guard
observationCamera: massless experiment/cosmic frame-track-orbit views with ship-state isolation
experimentNavigation: selected experiment fields + physical bounded-thrust rendezvous
spaceWeather: directional kinematic CME cones with explicit speed, arrival geometry, automatic seeded events, no MHD/radiation damage model, and save/load timeline continuity
scientificOverlays: target-centric circular-CR3BP L1/L2/L3 numerical equilibrium roots at live separation + equilateral L4/L5 geometry + Hill sphere + Roche limit + instantaneous orbital plane + live Newtonian gravity-vector samples; overlays remain diagnostic approximations and do not alter gravity
transitDrive: explicitly fictional spacecraft-only FRAME translation with swept massive-body clearance; ordinary celestial integration remains authoritative; manual exit matches target inertial velocity and supported normal body arrivals use an exit-only circular-orbit insertion calculation
boostDrive: explicitly speculative bounded 5,000 m/s² local propulsion mode; manual BOOST selection drops time warp to 1×
experimentLifecycle: active/complete lifecycle + retained final observation bounds + deterministic replay + active-particle-only 60× warp cap with safe restore
velocityVector: ship-view inertial velocity-direction HUD marker, separate from nose/reticle attitude
stellarRendering: layered seeded photosphere/granulation + additive corona + filament prominences + active regions + rare visual flare proxies
stellarPerceptualLod: preserve macro stellar phenomena at distance; reduce only sub-pixel/noisy micro detail and shift emphasis into scale-appropriate halo/prominence cues
stellarExposure: gentle apparent-angular-size exposure adaptation with close-star background suppression; HUD remains unaffected
transitArrivalVisual: short exponential release of fictional FRAME FOV/streak cues after disengage/arrival; physical Newtonian position and velocity are unchanged
systemMap: mobile-first live star → planet → moon navigation catalog with LOG SURVEY non-linear discovery view, TRUE SYSTEM linear inertial X/Z view, and TRUE LOCAL linear selected-planet/moon-family view; all modes read authoritative N-body positions and never create a second orbit model
discovery: persistent 0-3 layered scan depth per cosmic source; classification, signal/stability detail and final scientific/fictional status unlock progressively
anomalyLayer: 9-15 deterministic seeded free-space anomaly signals per system spanning speculative, anomalous and intentionally impossible/fictional reality classes; visuals never secretly become gravity sources
surfaceFoundation: data-driven multi-world landing/exploration over the canonical planetary-environment record: the accepted anomalous atmospheric home world remains intact; selected airless-rocky, tenuous-atmospheric-rocky and ice/volatile profiles now provide deterministic distinct surfaces without changing authoritative body/orbital state
surfacePhysicsBoundary: while landed, authoritative major-body N-body gravity continues at a forced 1× through the existing velocity-Verlet path while ShipDynamics/navigation are surface-constrained and not integrated; surface anomalies still do not create hidden gravity, teleportation or time effects; atmospheric entry/aerodynamics, fluid weather, rigid-body surface physics and ecosystems remain future layers
surfacePersistence: schema-1 surfaceSession payload preserves body/region identity, local x/z/yaw/pitch, scanned/selected POIs, weather timeline, body-fixed landing anchor/capture metadata and surfaceProfileId/surfaceModelVersion; restore now accepts local state only when saved body/profile identity matches the generated region so cross-world/profile state cannot leak
cockpitView: default-on low-obstruction camera-attached Three.js cockpit with four translucent smoked-glass CanvasTexture MFDs in landscape, including the live SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS pane; portrait compact-flight-deck mode keeps one central FLIGHT MFD with a low-alpha HUD-glass background and no opaque physical bezel, plus translucent NAV/FLIGHT/SCI/SYS shortcuts; hidden portrait objects remain excluded from picking; observation/surface auto-hide and schema-1 cockpitEnabled preference persistence are retained
surfaceWeather: persistent deterministic local weather remains unchanged on the legacy home profile; generalized tenuous-rocky surfaces use profile-restricted ordinary dust/frost events only, while airless/ice reference surfaces disable weather and wind scheduling. Weather presentation still applies no aerodynamic force or damage.
landedShip: upgraded lightweight spacecraft exterior with smoother hull, canopy, swept wings, twin engines, VTOL thrusters, landing gear, nav/strobe/landing lights, landing beacon and distance/boarding readout; visual surface representation remains separate from authoritative orbital ship physics while landed
surfaceHud: compact-by-default mobile exploration HUD with persistent expanded/collapsed state, always-available scan/sprint controls, details-only save/takeoff controls, and landed-only SKY PAUSE/RESUME plus body-fixed lat/lon, rotation phase, primary-star altitude/azimuth and geometric local solar-time diagnostics
landingLifecycle: explicit ORBIT -> DESCENDING -> LANDED -> ASCENDING -> ORBIT state machine with transition locking, near-ship boarding requirement, scripted VTOL descent/ascent visuals, cleanup-before-ORBIT commit, forced live-flight restoration, prograde return attitude, held-input reset, multi-frame orbital render verification and recovery fallback instead of half-transitioned states
landingRecovery: surface entry/ascent failures clean up renderer/UI/session state and fall back to a valid orbital state; successful takeoff force-restores running 1x ship flight, neutral input state and prograde attitude, then requires multiple verified orbital render frames before success
ascentHandoff: surface renderer ownership detaches before disposal; ASCENDING cleanup commits ORBIT only after local state is gone; held pointer controls are force-released; the ship returns in body-relative prograde attitude; three orbital frames render at zero simulation dt before ASCENT COMPLETE is announced; invariant misses recover without tripping the animation-loop fault latch
takeoffPhysicalDiagnostics: temporary compact ascent/orbit telemetry retained for iPhone Safari/WebKit release testing; renderer/backend and runtime performance/debug telemetry remain visible in ship view through the integrated SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS cockpit MFD and remain available in the ordinary top HUD when the cockpit is hidden
rendererBackendPolicy: WebGPURenderer remains the renderer family; iPhone/iPad-class WebKit forces its WebGL2 backend at boot for physical presentation-handoff isolation, while other platforms keep automatic WebGPU/WebGL2 selection; no live backend hot-swap
astronomicalObserver: one read-only canonical observer derives inertial position, look/local horizon bases, parent/anchor/altitude, simulation time and live major-body directions for ship, descent and surface modes; landed local-up/east/north now derive from a rotating body-fixed landing anchor when rotation metadata is available
skyContinuity: one deterministic inertial star catalog is reused in space and on surfaces; landed horizon projection is dynamically reprojected against the rotating body-fixed observer without reseeding or deleting catalog entries; atmospheric/daylight/weather visibility remains presentation-only
celestialApparentSize: planet/moon and stellar apparent angular radii use physical radius and observer range; distant UI markers remain separate from physical disk size
surfaceSkyTime: landed major-body celestial time advances at forced 1× when running and can now be explicitly paused/resumed from the surface DETAILS HUD; local exploration/weather remain separate and responsive while paused
magnetarPlacement: repeated LAB magnetars use deterministic golden-angle collision-safe offsets; gravity remains Newtonian and magnetic/MHD forces remain unmodeled
cockpitInteraction: every visible cockpit screen and physical key is functional; NAV opens the System Map, FLIGHT opens the existing Flight/System controls, SCIENCE opens Science, and SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS now opens a dedicated read-only Engineering/Diagnostics drawer instead of duplicating Flight/System; cockpit inputs dispatch existing app actions without duplicating simulation authority
cockpitAssetStrategy: procedural modular shell carried forward from v0.1.4.6.1.2; the diagnostics MFD is procedural CanvasTexture/geometry with no external cockpit asset, and presentation/control interfaces remain isolated so a later optimized GLB cockpit can replace the shell without rewriting flight/science systems
cockpitLighting: mobile-safe emissive-only panel accents plus live POWER/TARGET/NAV/PROPULSION/CAUTION indicators; no additional dynamic cockpit lights or physics state
cockpitDiagnostics: live renderer, FPS, physics/render time, ship speed, simulation time, seed, major/test counts, draw calls, prediction time and experiment telemetry are mirrored into the right-side translucent ship-mounted MFD and a dedicated read-only Engineering/Diagnostics drawer; the values remain sourced from existing app/renderer state and own no simulation authority
frameDrive: tap-toggle speculative spacecraft-only translation toward a locked body/COSMOS target; real-time frame-rate tiers step down near arrival; world N-body/particle simulation authority is untouched; local ship acceleration is suspended while active; manual disengage matches the target inertial velocity, while normal planet/moon/rogue-planet completion may hand off into a calculated circular osculating orbit before ordinary ShipDynamics/gravity resume
assetCachePolicy: HTML shell version-tags styles.css and src/main.js with build tag 152; main/app/renderer/cockpit module hops are also version-tagged so Safari/GitHub Pages do not mix the v0.1.5.2 shell with stale JavaScript.
planetaryRotation: fresh generated planets use orbital-relative v2 spin poles derived from parent-relative orbital angular momentum, with PRO/RETRO classification matching the physical spin pole; generated moons use parent+moon synchronous periods and face the parent at the rotation epoch. Existing schema-1 saves preserve serialized v1 rotation frames so body-fixed landing anchors do not move.
surfaceAstronomyDiagnostics: read-only surface DETAILS diagnostics derive from the same canonical astronomical observer and rotation model used by rendering: procedural body-fixed latitude/longitude, rotation phase, primary-star altitude/azimuth, and geometric local solar time from primary-star hour angle; no independent sky model or physics authority
planetaryNavigation: generated stars, planets and moons are first-class selectable NAV targets; planets/moons/rogues additionally expose canonical environment class, escape speed, stellar flux, radiative-equilibrium temperature, Bond albedo, atmosphere pressure/retention proxy, volatile/ice potential, surface family and tidal rotation state alongside existing live navigation diagnostics
frameOrbitArrival: normally completed FRAME travel to planets, moons and rogue planets hands back to Newtonian flight in a calculated instantaneous circular osculating orbit when a resolved window exists inside 47% of a conservative Hill-radius screening estimate based on the smaller of live separation and orbital pericenter; this is not a long-term N-body stability guarantee
landabilityFoundation: physical surface existence remains derived from canonical environment classification. v0.1.5.1 enables only the existing detailed atmospheric home world plus one deterministic qualifying airless-rocky moon proof surface; all other solids remain profile-classified but landing-disabled, and gas giants remain no-solid-surface.
frameSafetyRouting: deterministic live-body-anchored FRAME detours are used only when a direct swept segment would intersect another massive-body clearance guard; candidate bypass legs are checked against every massive-body guard, guard radii are never reduced, and celestial states are never moved by the route planner
generatorPhysicalConsistency: fresh gas giants use a bounded coherent bulk mass-density-radius proxy with density derived from authoritative mass/radius and a conservative Newtonian breakup-period floor; legacy saved gas geometry is preserved and only its dependent density is re-derived when needed.
roguePopulation: fresh generated rogue planets are guaranteed positive two-body specific orbital energy relative to the primary star; legacy saved rogue dynamical states are not rewritten.
collisionDetection: finite-radius swept sphere contact using the first relative-motion intersection root over each physics substep; contact position/velocity is linearly interpolated from a reusable flat previous-state buffer, then resolution occurs at that contact state with only the remaining substep drifted ballistically
impactConservation: merge/absorb paths conserve represented mass and linear momentum; fragment paths conserve represented 3-D linear momentum through COM-frame ejecta plus target recoil and cap represented ejecta/recoil kinetic energy to available COM impact energy; this is a bounded impact heuristic, not hydrodynamics/material fracture simulation
blackHoleAccretion: a black hole is the mandatory collision sink whenever one participant is a black hole; absorbed mass/momentum are accumulated and Schwarzschild radius is recomputed from the new mass
majorBodyStepControl: global major-body step ceiling remains 300 s for ordinary generated systems but is dynamically reduced from pair dynamical-time and crossing-time estimates for close/high-speed massive-body encounters such as LAB compact-object pairs
minorFieldCadence: minor test-particle field uses an accumulated simulation-time cadence at the configured 30 Hz when physics calls are finer than that interval, while large/high-warp substeps still update immediately; source start/end gravity states are retained for kick-drift-kick integration
collisionAllocationPolicy: major-body collision snapshots use reusable flat typed-array storage keyed by stable body topology; the pair scan remains scalar and avoids per-pair array allocation, allocating contact vectors only when an actual collision event is emitted
impactMaterialTyping: generated planetType gas aliases are normalized to gas-giant envelope response; gas planets do not use rocky crater estimation
postContactIntegration: collision state is resolved at interpolated first swept contact; the unresolved remainder of that one global substep is advanced ballistically before ordinary N-body integration resumes, rather than claiming a full event-driven force re-integration
celestialAppearance: read-only canonical apparent-radius, phase-angle, illuminated-fraction and finite-disk occultation geometry derived from authoritative observer/body/star positions; presentation consumes these values without simulation authority
planetMoonLighting: space planets and moons retain live star-direction MeshStandardMaterial terminator shading at physical render radius, with self-emission/readability shells removed from physical reflectors; star-light intensity remains exposure-normalized presentation rather than inverse-square radiative flux
surfaceCelestialDisks: surface stars use finite angular disks plus a separate non-physical glow cue; resolved planets/moons use phase-shaded 3D spheres on a monotonic compressed sky-shell depth while preserving authoritative sky direction and apparent angular size exactly
eclipseGeometry: finite apparent-disk overlap computes observer stellar occultation and body-centered stellar shadow using the dominant single foreground occulter; surface direct stellar light and daylight proxy respond to visible stellar fraction; overlapping multi-occulter disk unions are not yet solved
phaseRendering: phase angle and illuminated fraction are derived from star-target-observer geometry; surface planet/moon vertex lighting uses the canonical target-to-star direction as a Lambertian geometric proxy, not a detailed albedo/BRDF/radiative-transfer model
observationPlanner: read-only forward event search from the current simulation epoch using a cloned N-body ephemeris of the authoritative gravity-source bodies with the same direct Newtonian solver + velocity-Verlet integrator; 300 s coarse samples are locally refined to 10 s around star-body angular-separation minima and finite-disk eclipse coverage reuses the canonical celestialAppearance geometry
observationPlannerReference: selected planet/moon BODY CENTER by default; if the selected reference is the currently landed body, CURRENT LANDED SITE follows the saved body-fixed anchor/rotation and reports primary-star horizon visibility at predicted events
observationPlannerBoundary: planner state is cloned and never mutates authoritative bodies, ship, clock, save state, NAV target or FRAME; it does not predict future pilot motion, does not replay future collision/fragmentation resolution, and stops with an explicit numerical budget limit rather than silently degrading close-pair accuracy
observationPlannerHorizon: mobile UI offers 7/30/90/180-day forward searches; work is chunked across animation frames, event results are limited/sorted, and alignments outside 5 degrees are not listed unless finite stellar-disk overlap occurs
observationPlannerMobileLayout: planner-local iOS text autosizing suppression + content-sized event cards + dedicated inertial results scrolling; planner math/ephemeris behavior unchanged
planetaryEnvironmentModel: canonical read-only planetary-environment-v1 solver separates hard derived physics (bulk density, surface gravity, escape velocity, stellar flux and radiative-equilibrium temperature) from deterministic seeded formation assumptions (Bond albedo, volatile inventory and atmospheric inventory); no orbital/body state is mutated
planetaryEnvironmentFormation: independent per-body seeded-formation-v1 RNG stream so environment metadata cannot perturb legacy orbital generation; schema-1 saves preserve serialized environment formation metadata and older saves deterministically backfill missing fields without replacing mass/radius/orbit/rotation
planetaryAtmosphereBoundary: solid-world pressure is a seeded atmospheric-inventory + Jeans-style thermal-retention + generic heavy-volatile gas-phase-availability proxy; greenhouse climate, detailed chemistry/condensation, EUV/stellar-wind escape, photochemistry and radiative transfer are not solved; gas giants expose a deep H/He envelope with no invented surface pressure
planetaryEnvironmentClassification: derived solid/gas surface existence plus rocky/dry/volatile-rich/ice-rich/hot terrestrial, moon, rogue and gas-giant environment classes; solid surface capability is explicitly separate from whether the generalized multi-world surface engine exists
surfaceArchitecture: surface profile family classification remains separate from environment classification and recognizes ATMOSPHERIC_ROCKY, AIRLESS_ROCKY and ICE_VOLATILE. v0.1.5.2 enables a bounded deterministic exploration set: legacy home + at most one airless rocky reference moon + one contrasting rocky planet + one ice/volatile world when qualifying candidates exist.
surfaceProofWorld: ORIGIN-001 reference surfaces are Caelum-4361 d (legacy atmospheric home), Caelum-4361 f-A (airless rocky), Caelum-4361 e (cold tenuous-atmosphere rocky), and Caelum-4361 h-A (airless cryogenic ice/rock). Selection is deterministic from canonical environment records and does not consume orbital RNG.
surfaceVacuumModel: airless rocky and qualifying cryogenic ice surfaces disable fog, clouds, wind and surface-weather scheduling; black daylight sky retains canonical stars/planets/moons and direct stellar lighting. Regolith/ice colors, roughness, fractures, craters and contaminants remain deterministic presentation/geology proxies.
surfaceTakeoffOrbit: legacy home-world takeoff preserves the accepted 5-radius return path. Generalized surfaces preserve the departing session through cleanup, reconstruct the current inertial radial direction from the rotating body-fixed landing anchor, then reuse the existing Hill-screened circular-orbit insertion planner for safe local handoff.
portraitCockpitLayout: portrait ship view keeps the wide canopy and one readable central FLIGHT MFD, hides landscape-only side MFDs/diagnostics mount/physical key row, exposes direct NAV/FLIGHT/SCI/SYS shortcuts through existing app actions, recomposes LOOK/thrust/bottom controls around iPhone safe areas, and restores the accepted full four-MFD cockpit automatically in landscape; no simulation authority or save state is owned by orientation layout
multiWorldExploration: bounded v0.1.5.2 exploration set supports FRAME/orbit -> LAND -> deterministic body-specific surface -> save/load -> TAKEOFF for selected rocky/airless/ice worlds; ORIGIN-001 adds Caelum-4361 e and h-A while other solid bodies remain locked and rogues stay excluded until rotation modeling is complete.
surfaceRenderingProfiles: generalized rocky profile uses canonical pressure/gravity/equilibrium temperature with a low-density atmosphere/fog presentation proxy and ordinary dust/frost weather; ice/volatile profile uses canonical albedo/ice potential with lower-roughness cryogenic terrain, bright ice shards/dark ejecta proxies and no atmosphere/weather on the ORIGIN reference moon.
